title: Fair money splitting
goal: Implement two functions in src/split.js: splitAmount(cents, parts) and splitByWeights(cents, weights) to split money fairly using integer division with remainder handling.

steps.title: Implement fair money splitting functions
steps.detail: src/split.js exports splitAmount(cents, parts) and splitByWeights(cents, weights). Amounts are integer numbers of cents. splitAmount splits cents into parts shares that differ by at most one cent and add up exactly to cents; the extra cents go to the FIRST shares one each; a negative amount is split the same way on its absolute value and every share is negative (-100 into 3 is [-34, -33, -33]); parts that is not a positive integer throws a RangeError; cents that is not an integer throws a TypeError. splitByWeights splits cents in proportion to non-negative integer weights with the largest-remainder method: each share starts as the floor of its exact proportion, the cents still unassigned go one each to the shares with the largest fractional remainders, ties go to the earlier index; the shares add up exactly to cents; a weight array that is empty, has a negative or non-integer weight, or sums to zero throws a RangeError; negative cents are handled like splitAmount (split the absolute value, negate every share). Examples: splitAmount(100,3) is [34,33,33]; splitAmount(1,3) is [1,0,0]; splitAmount(0,4) is [0,0,0,0]; splitAmount(10,5) is [2,2,2,2,2]; splitAmount(-100,3) is [-34,-33,-33]; splitAmount(100,0) throws RangeError; splitAmount(1.5,2) throws TypeError; splitByWeights(100,[1,1,1]) is [34,33,33]; splitByWeights(10,[1,2,3]) is [2,3,5]; splitByWeights(5,[1,1]) is [3,2]; splitByWeights(100,[0,1,1]) is [0,50,50]; splitByWeights(7,[1,0,0]) is [7,0,0]; splitByWeights(100,[0,0]) throws RangeError; splitByWeights(-10,[1,2,3]) is [-2,-3,-5]. Export with module.exports = { splitAmount, splitByWeights } (CommonJS). Add tests in test/split.test.js (node:test) covering every rule and example.

steps.title: Run the whole test suite
steps.detail: Run npm test. Change nothing unless it fails; fix only failures that this plan's change caused.
